big: Dadi has ₹10 lakh to keep safe for five years. She could put it all in one deposit, one bond or one fund. There is a smarter way to spread it.

lines: Beta, I do not want to lose sleep. How do I keep it safe and still earn something?
Match the choice to your goal, spread the money, and stagger the end dates. Let us build it step by step.

alt: A bar split into four equal parts that end in one, two, three and four years
caps: One deposit ending in four years locks all the money until the end.
A ladder splits it into four parts ending in one, two, three and four years.
Each year one part comes due, so some cash is always close at hand.
Each part can be renewed at the going rate, so you are not stuck with one rate.

intro: Run through this for any deposit, bond or debt fund.
rows: When do I need the money, and can I handle a dip?
Not all with one bank, company or fund
Read the credit rating and what the fund holds
note: Keep emergency money separate, in simple and easy-to-reach places.

q: Rohan needs money for a wedding in two years and wants the highest advertised rate. What does goal matching say?
opts: Pick the highest rate, whatever it holds, since returns are what matter
Choose a very long bond fund, since it pays the most each year
Choose something steady that fits two years, even if its rate is lower
Wait until the wedding is closer before deciding anything about it
why: A very high rate usually carries higher risk, which is a poor fit for a near, fixed need.
A long bond fund swings the most when rates change, so it is a poor fit for two years.
A two-year goal needs steadiness more than the top rate, since a dip could land at the wrong time.
Waiting leaves the money idle. Planning early gives time to choose a fitting option.

q: Dadi puts ₹10 lakh into four deposits ending in 1, 2, 3 and 4 years. What is the main benefit of this ladder?
opts: Some money comes due every year, giving cash access and a chance to renew
It raises the interest rate on every deposit above the going rate
It removes any chance of losing money at the bank, even above the limit
It makes all the interest on these deposits tax-exempt in each year
why: Each year a part ends, so cash is near, and it can be renewed at the then-current rate.
A ladder does not raise the rate. Each deposit earns the rate that applied when it was made.
A ladder spreads end dates. It does not remove bank risk, so the insurance limit still matters.
Interest remains taxable whatever the ladder, so no tax saving comes from the structure.

q: Meena lends ₹6 lakh, all of it to one company through a single bond. What is the main weakness?
opts: The interest will be lower, since big loans always pay less
The bond cannot be repaid, since it is larger than the usual size
There is no weakness, because a single rated bond is as safe as any
One failure could cost her much of the money, so spreading is wiser
why: Loan size does not set the rate. The borrower's risk and the term mostly do.
Bonds of this size are routinely repaid. The size is not the weakness here.
A rating lowers risk but cannot remove it, so concentration is still a weakness.
With everything lent to one borrower, a default hits the whole sum, and spreading limits the damage.

q: Before buying a debt fund, Rohan reads its list of holdings. What is he checking?
opts: Whether the fund's name is easy to remember when he talks about it later
Which borrowers it lends to, and whether the credit quality is high
How many people work at the fund house, since more staff means less risk
The colour scheme of the fund's factsheet, since bright ones mean safe
why: A name tells nothing about risk. The holdings tell you what the fund really owns.
The list shows which borrowers the fund lends to, so he can judge credit quality.
Staff numbers do not reveal the risk of the fund's holdings.
Design has no link to risk. The holdings and their ratings do.

pts: Match the tool to the goal and the time you have.
Ladders and spreading across banks and borrowers reduce risk.
Read the rating and the holdings before you invest.
